newsitem.title: DENMARK: Buyer dearth hits Danish shares, more falls ahead.
newsitem.headline: Buyer dearth hits Danish shares, more falls ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower on Thursday hit by an acute lack of buyers in a dull market, with dealers fearing fresh falls ahead unless Wall Street makes a major recovery.
"Things can change quickly of course but things look none to good for tomorrow. There are few serious investors in the market, only marketmakers and short-term buyers," one dealer complained.
The KFX top-20 index closed 1.80 point down at 152.73, while the KFX March future fell 1.85 point to 152.10 with 880 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Superfos was in focus as it announced a bumper 1996 result, but the share closed only one crown up at 775 after peaking at 796.

In the takeover battle for Danish roadbuilder Phoenix, Superfos, which had offered 808 million crowns for the company, said it would not raise its bid and Phoenix later recommended its shareholders to accept a rival 820 million crown bid from Norway's Rieber & Son.
Phoenix closed five crowns down at 665.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.046 billion crowns.
